MUSICAL THEATREFiddler on the Roof ★★★★★Her Majesty’s Theatre, until December 27

Fiddler on the Roof has strummed through thousands of performances since its first run in 1964 on Broadway and its Australian premiere three years later. This latest version comes from director Jordan Fein’s 2024 London season.

Its decades-long popularity is a testament to the musical’s enduring themes of generational conflict and the inevitability of change. There are, of course, also the rousing songs, joyful choreography, and characters who are idiosyncratic enough to appear as individuals rather than simply emblems of stasis or progress.

Set in 1905 in a small village in Russia, it follows the hardscrabble life of a Jewish milkman, Tevye (Troy Sussman) and his wife, Golde (Alexis Fishman) as they uphold rigorous traditions handed down about marriage, gender roles and social interactions.

Unfortunately, three of their five daughters are determined to thwart the matchmaker’s choices. As a parent, Tevye knows that if they choose their spouses unwisely, their fates are as precarious as the titular fiddler trying to ply his craft on a roof. The heart of the production rests upon whether Tevye bends to their autonomous desires or remains patriarchally inflexible.

Sussman plays his role with humour, warmth, and commanding gravitas. Fishman’s bossy, sharp-tongued Golde is a perfect foil. You know she’s the one wielding the real power in their relationship.

Tzeitel (Freya Boltman), Hodel (Ellen Ebbs), Chava (Caity Plummer) are the daughters whose love and respect for their father mean their rebellion is necessarily tempered by the push and pull of filial duty and antagonism. All three acquit their roles with the earnestness and passion of young women desperate for independence.
